result.topic_en: Draft passages on representing algebraic functions of $s$ and $z$ as quotients of products of theta functions, noting that the quotient must stay unchanged under substitutions of theta arguments, that the simplest such quotients are irrational (radical-type) functions involving $m$-th roots of unity, and that other quotients can be written in the form $\vartheta(u_1-\Sigma\alpha^{(1)}, \ldots)$.

methods.what: A quotient of even theta products changes only by a constant factor; for it to be algebraic the factor must be an $m$-th root of unity, so its $m$-th power is an unramified, hence rational, function
methods.quote:

sein soll
